# API index (generated by tools/gen_api.py, do not edit)

Public declarations of the portable code, header by header. Engine parameters are in `docs/catalog.md`; conventions and rules in `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/adding_an_engine.md`.

## `dsp/synth.h`
the single public API of the synthesis engine. The calls on one instance must come from one thread at a time (normally the audio thread): a multi-threaded host forwards MIDI and parameter changes to it through a lock-free queue (see host/). Parameter names, ranges and help: docs/catalog.md (generated from the descriptor tables).
- types: `synth_engine_t`
- constants: `SYNTH_PARAM_GLOBAL` = 256, `SYNTH_PART_PARAM` = 512, `SYNTH_MOD_PARAM` = 1024
- `size_t synth_size(void)` — Bytes one instance needs (its state and its effect memory).
- `synth_t *synth_create(void *mem, size_t bytes, float sample_rate)` — Places an instance in mem (synth_size() bytes, 16-byte aligned) and initializes it; NULL if mem does not fit.
- `synth_t *synth_default(void)` — The static instance (DSP_FAST_DATA state, DSP_LARGE_DATA effect memory); call synth_init on it first.
- `void synth_part_engine(synth_t *s, int part, synth_engine_t engine)` — Sets the engine of a part (SYNTH_ENGINE_NONE switches it off); same fade as synth_set_engine.
- `void synth_part_param(synth_t *s, int part, int id, float value)` — Sets a parameter of a part: an engine parameter id (0..255), a SYNTH_PART_* id or a modulation id (SYNTH_MOD_PARAM + index); value normalized in [0, 1] like synth_set_param. Global ids (SYNTH_PARAM_GLOBAL..) are accep...
- `void synth_part_kit(synth_t *s, int part, const void *kit, size_t bytes)` — Gives a part a sample kit (format: core/kit.h), played by the engines that play samples (sampler). The kit is read where it lies, never copied: it must stay valid and unchanged until the part gets another one (or NULL...
- `void synth_init(synth_t *s, float sample_rate)` — Initializes all state (no allocation). Default engine: SYNTH_ENGINE_VA, effects off.
- `void synth_set_engine(synth_t *s, synth_engine_t engine)` — Switches engine. If voices are sounding, a one-block fade-out precedes the switch; subsequent events wait until the switch is done. Effects keep running (tails continue).
- `void synth_midi(synth_t *s, const uint8_t *msg, int len, int sample_offset)` — Complete MIDI message (status + data, running status already resolved), 1 to 3 bytes; real-time clock messages (1 byte) drive the tempo when SYNTH_PARAM_CLOCK = midi. sample_offset: offset in samples from the start of...
- `void synth_set_param(synth_t *s, int id, float value)` — Sets a parameter; value is normalized in [0, 1] (descriptor curve). Smoothed internally.
- `void synth_render(synth_t *s, float *L, float *R, int n)` — Produces n stereo samples (any n; split internally into SYNTH_BLOCK blocks).

## `dsp/core/denormal.h`
enables flush-to-zero (denormal numbers set to zero) for the current thread. Apple Silicon: FZ bit (24) of the FPCR register. Cortex-M7: FZ bit (24) of FPSCR. The setting is per thread: synth_render calls it on every entry (cost: 2 instructions).
- `void dsp_denormals_off(void)` — STM32 note: inside an interrupt, FPSCR is reloaded from FPU->FPDSCR. The board code must therefore also do FPU->FPDSCR |= FPU_FPDSCR_FZ_Msk at init.

## `dsp/core/dsp.h`
definitions shared by the whole engine: block size, memory placement (DTCM/ITCM on STM32), small inline helpers (clamping, xorshift random, ramps, NaN guard). No dependency beyond <stdint.h> and <stddef.h>.
- types: `dsp_bits_t`
- constants: `SYNTH_BLOCK` = 32
- `float dsp_minf(float a, float b)`
- `float dsp_maxf(float a, float b)`
- `float dsp_absf(float x)`
- `float dsp_clampf(float x, float lo, float hi)` — a NaN comes out as lo (never propagated into indices or filter coefficients)
- `int dsp_clampi(int x, int lo, int hi)`
- `int dsp_isfinite(float x)` — True if x is neither NaN nor infinite (exponent not 255).
- `uint32_t dsp_rand_u32(uint32_t *s)` — ---- Deterministic random: xorshift32 (Marsaglia). The state must never be 0. ----
- `float dsp_rand_bipolar(uint32_t *s)` — Value in [-1, 1).
- `float dsp_rand_unipolar(uint32_t *s)` — Value in [0, 1).
- `uint32_t dsp_seed(uint32_t x)` — Mixes an arbitrary seed into a valid (non-zero) xorshift state.
- `void dsp_ramp_mul(float *restrict x, float g0, float g1, int n)` — x[i] *= g, g going from g0 (excluded) to g1 (reached on the last sample).
- `void dsp_ramp_mac(float *restrict acc, const float *restrict x, float g0, float g1, int n)` — acc[i] += x[i] * g, same ramp.
- `void dsp_guard_block(float *x, int n, uint32_t *count)` — ---- NaN/Inf guard (debug build only: SYNTH_NAN_GUARD) ---- Host: immediate stop (__builtin_trap) to catch the bug in the debugger. Board: zero the block and increment the counter.

## `dsp/core/fastmath.h`
fast math functions for the audio path, with no libm calls. Sine: 2048-point table + linear interpolation (error < 1.2e-6). exp2: rounding + 6th-order Taylor on [-0.5, 0.5] (relative error < 3e-7); log2: atanh series; tanh: (3,2) Pade approximant, clamped to +/-1 beyond |x| = 3.
- constants: `FM_SIN_BITS` = 11, `FM_SIN_SIZE`, `FM_PI`, `FM_TWO_PI`, `FM_LN2`, `FM_LOG2E`
- data: `const float fm_sin_table[FM_SIN_SIZE + 1]`
- `float fm_frac(float x)` — Fractional part in [0, 1). Assumes |x| < 2^31.
- `float fm_sin(float phase)` — sin(2*pi*phase), phase expressed in cycles (any value).
- `float fm_sin_pos(float phase)` — fm_sin for a phase known to be >= 0 (|phase| < 2^31): the same value, without fm_frac's negative branch.
- `float fm_cos(float phase)`
- `float fm_exp2(float x)` — 2^x, x clamped to [-126, 126].
- `float fm_log2(float x)` — log2(x) for x > 0 (returns -126 otherwise).
- `float fm_exp(float x)`
- `float fm_mtof(float note)` — MIDI note number (fractional) -> frequency in Hz (A4 = 69 = 440 Hz).
- `float fm_db2lin(float db)` — dB -> linear gain, and the inverse.
- `float fm_lin2db(float g)`
- `float fm_tan_pi(float x)` — tan(pi*x) for x in [0, 0.49] (prewarping for TPT filters).
- `float fm_tanh(float x)` — tanh(x): (3,2) Pade, continuous and with zero derivative at |x| = 3.

## `dsp/core/fft.h`
in-place complex radix-2 FFT for init-time work (band-limiting wavetables). Not for the audio path. Twiddles come from the fastmath sine table (no libm), error ~1e-6. Reference: Cooley & Tukey (1965), iterative decimation in time with bit-reversal permutation.
- `void fft_complex(float *re, float *im, int n, int inverse)` — n: power of two. inverse = 1 computes the unscaled inverse transform (divide by n yourself).

## `dsp/core/kit.h`
a sample kit in memory: the samples the sampler engine plays, read where they lie (flash, SDRAM, a file loaded by the host) without being copied. Format "OIDK" version 1, little-endian: header (8 bytes) "OIDK", version u16, count u16 (at most KIT_MAX) directory count entries of 32 bytes {name[20], note u8, flags u8, reserved u16, offset u32, frames u32} samples 16-bit signed mono PCM at 48 kHz, each at its offset (bytes from the start of the kit, even) One sample per MIDI note. Transported to the boards by the board link (docs/link.md).
- types: `kit_entry_t`
- constants: `KIT_VERSION` = 1u, `KIT_HEADER` = 8, `KIT_ENTRY` = 32, `KIT_MAX` = 128, `KIT_NAME` = 20
- `int kit_count(const uint8_t *kit, size_t size)` — Checks a kit: magic, version, every sample inside it. Returns its number of samples, -1 if invalid.
- `void kit_entry(const uint8_t *kit, int k, kit_entry_t *e)` — Entry k of a valid kit.
- `const int16_t *kit_samples(const uint8_t *kit, const kit_entry_t *e)` — The samples of an entry (the kit must be 2-byte aligned; the PCM is little-endian like every target).
- `int kit_write_directory(uint8_t *kit, const kit_entry_t *e, int count)` — Writes the header and the directory (KIT_HEADER + count * KIT_ENTRY bytes); the caller writes the samples at the entries' offsets. Returns the directory's size, -1 if count is out of range.

## `dsp/core/smooth.h`
parameter smoothing with a one-pole low-pass filter, evaluated once per block (control rate). Typical time constant: 5 ms. Consumers then interpolate linearly sample by sample.
- types: `smooth_t`
- `void smooth_init(smooth_t *s, float tau_s, float rate_hz, float initial)` — tau_s: time constant in seconds; rate_hz: rate at which smooth_next is called.
- `float smooth_next(smooth_t *s, float target)`
- `void smooth_snap(smooth_t *s, float v)`

## `dsp/osc/fm_op.h`
one FM operator: sine oscillator with a phase-modulation input (phase modulation, as on the classic digital FM instruments), frequency and amplitude interpolated linearly over each block. Algorithms (who modulates whom) belong to the engine. Reference: J. Chowning, "The Synthesis of Complex Audio Spectra by Means of Frequency Modulation" (JAES 1973).
- types: `fm_op_t`
- `void fm_op_reset(fm_op_t *o, float phase)` — New note: phase, and no pitch glide from the previous note (the frequency starts on its target; the amplitude ramps from zero over the first block, which is what avoids a click).
- `void fm_op_block(fm_op_t *o, float inc1, float amp1, float inv_n)` — Once per block: ramp to frequency inc1 (cycles per sample) and amplitude amp1 over the block (inv_n = 1/n).
- `float fm_op_tick(fm_op_t *o, float pm)` — One sample with phase modulation pm (cycles).

## `dsp/osc/noise.h`
uniform white noise in [-1, 1) via xorshift32 (Marsaglia 2003). Deterministic: same seed -> bit-identical sequence.
- types: `noise_t`
- `void noise_init(noise_t *z, uint32_t seed)`
- `void noise_process(noise_t *z, float *restrict out, int n)`

## `dsp/osc/polyblep.h`
anti-aliased oscillator: saw and pulse (PWM) via 2-point polyBLEP, triangle via 2-point polyBLAMP, sine via table. Reference: Valimaki, Pekonen, Nam, "Perceptually informed synthesis of bandlimited classical waveforms using integrated polynomial interpolation" (JASA 2012); Esqueda et al. (polyBLAMP).
- types: `osc_wave_t`, `osc_t`
- `void osc_init(osc_t *o, float sample_rate)`
- `void osc_reset(osc_t *o, float phase)` — Restarts from a given phase; the pitch of the next block does not glide from the old one.
- `void osc_set_wave(osc_t *o, osc_wave_t w)`
- `void osc_set(osc_t *o, float freq_hz, float pw)` — Target frequency (Hz) and pulse width (0..1): interpolated over the next block.
- `void osc_process(osc_t *o, float *restrict out, int n)`
- `float osc_blep(float t, float dt, float idt)` — polyBLEP residual of a rising unit step. idt ~= 1/dt (interpolated, hence the clamps).
- `float osc_blamp(float t, float dt, float idt)` — polyBLAMP residual of a unit slope break (per sample).

## `dsp/osc/selfosc.h`
self-oscillating nonlinear oscillator (Van der Pol with a Duffing term), forced by a sine at the note frequency: x'' - mu (1 - x^2) x' + x + beta x^3 = F cos(phi_note), in time scaled by the natural angular frequency. mu (drive) morphs a pure sine (mu ~ 0) into a relaxation wave (square / pulse-like, mu ~ 5); beta (stiffness) makes the pitch depend on the amplitude; F (entrain) locks the oscillator onto the note. The pitch drop of the Van der Pol cycle with mu is compensated by a precomputed table. Integrated with an exact damping step between two half kicks (Strang splitting, leapfrog) at 4x the sample rate, decimated by two half-band stages. References: B. van der Pol (1926); A. Pikovsky, M. Rosenblum, J. Kurths, "Synchronization" (2001).
- types: `selfosc_table_t`, `selfosc_t`
- constants: `SELFOSC_MU_MAX` = 5.0f
- data: `const selfosc_table_t selfosc_table`
- `void selfosc_table_init(selfosc_table_t *t)` — Measures the pitch of the free Van der Pol cycle for every table entry: 1.26 million integration steps, too slow for an engine init on the board. It is the generator of selfosc_table (and its test), not runtime code.
- `float selfosc_ratio(const selfosc_table_t *t, float mu)` — Frequency of the free cycle relative to the natural frequency, for drive mu (interpolated).
- `void selfosc_reset(selfosc_t *s, float x0)`
- `void selfosc_process(selfosc_t *s, float sample_rate, float f_nat, float f_force, float mu, float beta, float force, float *out, int n)` — Adds nothing: writes n samples. f_nat: natural frequency (Hz); f_force: forcing frequency (Hz); mu: drive 0..5; beta: stiffness; force: forcing amplitude; out: about +/-1.

## `dsp/osc/splay.h`
plays a 16-bit sample at any speed, forwards or backwards, between a start and an end point, once or in a loop. Band-limited interpolation: a Kaiser-windowed sinc whose cutoff follows the speed (at speed r > 1 it drops to 1/r of the source band), so a sample played faster does not alias (J. O. Smith, "Digital Audio Resampling", bandlimited interpolation). A one-shot fades out over its last SPLAY_FADE frames, so an end point inside the sound does not click.
- types: `splay_t`
- data: `const float splay_kernel[SPLAY_ZC * SPLAY_RES + 2]`
- `void splay_init(splay_t *p)` — Silent until splay_start.
- `void splay_start(splay_t *p, const int16_t *data, int32_t frames, float start, float end, int reverse, int loop)` — Starts playing data (frames samples) from start to end (fractions 0..1 of the sample; end is pushed past start), backwards from end to start when reverse, around [start, end) when loop.
- `void splay_set_loop(splay_t *p, int loop)` — Loop on or off while playing (a released note leaves its loop and plays to the end).
- `int splay_process(splay_t *p, float *out, int n, float rate0, float rate1)` — Writes n samples (full scale 1.0) at a speed (1 = original pitch) ramping from rate0 to rate1 across the block, clamped to [0, SPLAY_RATE_MAX]; zeros once finished. Returns 1 while playing.

## `dsp/osc/supersaw.h`
stack of up to 7 detuned polyBLEP saws ("supersaw"), with irregular detune spacing (no common beat period, cf. A. Szabo, "How to Emulate the Super Saw", 2010), random start phases, loudness-normalized side mix, and one slow desynchronized LFO per saw that moves its detune ("motion"). Per-saw LFOs run at control rate; pitch is interpolated by each saw over the block.
- types: `supersaw_t`
- constants: `SUPERSAW_MAX` = 7
- `void supersaw_init(supersaw_t *s, float sample_rate, uint32_t seed)`
- `void supersaw_reset(supersaw_t *s)` — New note: random phases for every saw and new random LFO rates/phases; no pitch glide.
- `void supersaw_set(supersaw_t *s, float freq_hz, float detune_cents, float side, float motion_cents, float motion_hz, int count, int block)` — freq_hz: centre pitch; detune_cents: outermost saw offset; side: level of the 6 side saws (0..1); motion_cents / motion_hz: depth and rate of the per-saw detune LFOs; count: 1, 3, 5 or 7 saws. Call once per block, bef...
- `void supersaw_process(supersaw_t *s, float *restrict out, int n)`

## `dsp/osc/wavetable.h`
band-limited wavetable oscillator. A table is WT_FRAMES single-cycle frames; each frame is stored as WT_LEVELS mipmaps (one per octave, 512 harmonics down to 1), built at init by FFT from a generator function. Playback: linear interpolation inside a frame and between neighbouring frames ("position"), mip level chosen per block so harmonics stay below 0.55 x SR (what folds back lands above 20 kHz), unison stack, and phase warps: hard sync (polyBLEP-corrected reset), bend, mirror, phase modulation and ring modulation by an external signal. References: P. Burk, "Band Limited Oscillators Using Wave Table Synthesis" (Audio Anecdotes, 2004); V. Valimaki et al. on polyBLEP for the sync discontinuity.
- types: `wt_warp_t`, `wt_osc_t`, `wt_osc_set_t`
- constants: `WT_LEVELS` = 10, `WT_TABLE_FLOATS`, `WT_SCRATCH_FLOATS`, `WT_UNISON_MAX` = 8
- `void wt_build(float *table, wt_gen_fn gen, float *scratch)` — Builds one table (WT_TABLE_FLOATS) from a generator. Init only (FFT); scratch: WT_SCRATCH_FLOATS.
- `void wt_osc_reset(wt_osc_t *o, uint32_t *rng)` — New note: random start phases from rng (unison voices must not start in phase).
- `void wt_osc_process(wt_osc_t *o, const float *table, const wt_osc_set_t *s, float inv_sr, const float *mod, float *out, int n)` — Adds n samples into out. mod: external signal for the FM and RING warps (may be NULL otherwise). Position and level ramp linearly over the block; warp and pitch are block-constant.

## `dsp/osc/wt_factory.h`
the built-in wavetables, all generated from formulas (no sampled material): classic shapes, pulse width, hard sync, additive harmonics, vowel formants, sine folding, phase-modulation growl, resonant window (phase-distortion style) and random digital spectra. Built once into a caller-provided memory block (init only).
- data: `const char *const wt_factory_names[]`
- `int wt_factory_build(float *mem, size_t floats)` — Builds as many tables as fit in mem (floats); returns that count (0 if not even one fits).
- `const float *wt_factory_table(const float *mem, int built, int i)` — Table i, or table 0 if i was not built.

## `dsp/filter/comb.h`
feedback comb filter: y = x + g * damp(y delayed by sr / f), peaks at the multiples of f (g > 0) or at the odd multiples of f / 2 (g < 0: hollow). The delay is read with 4-point Hermite interpolation and glides over each block, so the comb can wander (modulated tuning) without zipper or clicks; a one-pole low-pass in the loop makes the high peaks decay faster. Output normalized so the peaks stay near unity. Delays longer than the buffer play an octave up (same harmonic series). Reference: J. O. Smith, "Physical Audio Signal Processing", feedback comb filters; Hermite interpolation after Niemitalo (2001).
- types: `comb_t`
- `void comb_init(comb_t *c, float sample_rate)`
- `void comb_reset(comb_t *c)`
- `void comb_set(comb_t *c, float freq_hz, float feedback, float damping)` — freq_hz: the comb's fundamental; feedback -0.98..0.98; damping 0..1 (0 = bright repeats).
- `void comb_process(comb_t *c, const float *in, float *out, int n)` — in and out may be the same buffer.

## `dsp/filter/dcblock.h`
DC blocker: 1-pole / 1-zero high-pass at ~10 Hz, y[n] = x[n] - x[n-1] + R*y[n-1] with R = 1 - 2*pi*fc/SR (J. O. Smith, "Introduction to Digital Filters").
- types: `dcblock_t`
- `void dcblock_init(dcblock_t *d, float sample_rate)`
- `void dcblock_reset(dcblock_t *d)`
- `void dcblock_process(dcblock_t *d, const float *in, float *out, int n)` — in and out may be the same.

## `dsp/filter/formant.h`
vowel filter: three band-pass TPT state-variable filters in parallel at the formants of a vowel, morphing continuously a -> e -> i -> o -> u, shiftable in octaves (smaller or larger "throat") with a sharpness control. Coefficients glide over each block (the SVF interpolates), so the vowel can move. Formant values: G. Peterson & H. Barney (1952), average adult vowels.
- types: `formant_t`
- `void formant_init(formant_t *f, float sample_rate)`
- `void formant_reset(formant_t *f)`
- `void formant_set(formant_t *f, float vowel, float shift_oct, float q)` — vowel 0..1 (a, e, i, o, u), shift in octaves (0 = adult voice), q = sharpness of the formants (2..20).
- `void formant_process(formant_t *f, const float *in, float *out, int n)` — in and out may be the same buffer.

## `dsp/filter/halfband.h`
2x and 4x oversampling for nonlinear stages: polyphase half-band FIR up (one input sample -> two at the double rate) and down (two -> one), 47 taps, Kaiser beta 8, about -56 dB stopband; 11.5 samples of latency each way. 4x cascades two 2x stages (the same filter works at any rate: its cutoff is a quarter of its own rate); the inner stage adds 5.75 base samples each way. Used by the ladder and the screaming 2-pole filter around their saturating feedback. Reference: polyphase half-band decimation/interpolation (e.g. R. Lyons, "Understanding DSP", ch. 10).
- types: `hb2x_t`, `hb4x_t`
- `void hb2x_reset(hb2x_t *h)`
- `void hb2x_up(hb2x_t *h, float in, float *a, float *b)` — One input sample -> two samples at 2x: *a first, then *b.
- `float hb2x_down(hb2x_t *h, float ya, float yb)` — Two samples at 2x (ya first) -> one output sample.
- `void hb4x_reset(hb4x_t *h)`
- `void hb4x_up(hb4x_t *h, float in, float out[4])` — One input sample -> four at 4x, in order.
- `float hb4x_down(hb4x_t *h, const float y[4])` — Four samples at 4x -> one output sample.
- `int hb_factor(int factor)` — The oversampling factor a caller asks for, made valid: 1, 2 or 4.

## `dsp/filter/ladder.h`
4-pole transistor-ladder low-pass in zero-delay-feedback (TPT) form, with a saturating input stage, resonance up to self-oscillation, 24/18/12 dB outputs and optional 2x oversampling (47-tap polyphase half-band, -56 dB stopband) for the nonlinearity. References: V. Zavalishin, "The Art of VA Filter Design", ch. 5 (ladder, zero-delay feedback); A. Huovilainen, "Non-linear digital implementation of the Moog ladder filter" (DAFx 2004).
- types: `ladder_mode_t`, `ladder_t`
- `void ladder_init(ladder_t *l, float sample_rate)`
- `void ladder_reset(ladder_t *l)`
- `void ladder_set_mode(ladder_t *l, ladder_mode_t mode)`
- `void ladder_set_oversampling(ladder_t *l, int factor)` — Runs the filter at 1, 2 or 4 times the sample rate: higher = less aliasing from the drive and the saturated resonance (cleaner self-oscillation high up), at about 2.5x then 5x the cost of 1x. Changing it restarts the ...
- `void ladder_set(ladder_t *l, float cutoff_hz, float resonance, float drive)` — cutoff in Hz; resonance 0..1 (self-oscillation from ~0.95); drive 0..1 (input saturation).
- `void ladder_set_compensation(ladder_t *l, float amount)` — How much of the passband loss caused by the resonance is made up (default 0.35; call before ladder_set). 0 = none, as in the transistor ladder itself: turning the resonance up thins the bass.
- `void ladder_process(ladder_t *l, const float *in, float *out, int n)` — in and out may be the same buffer. Coefficients are interpolated over the call (one block).
- `void ladder_process_fb(ladder_t *l, const float *in, const float *post, float fb, float hp_coef, float *state, float *out, int n)` — The same with the output fed back into the input, one sample late, through the caller's post gain (the amplifier that follows the filter): in[i] + fb * hp(out[i-1] * post[i-1]). hp is a one-pole high-pass (hp_coef = 1...

## `dsp/filter/resonator.h`
complex one-pole resonator: z <- (c + i s) z + g x, output = Im(z). A rotation by the mode frequency times a decay radius per sample, so frequency and T60 are exact and it never goes unstable (|c + i s| < 1). One mode of a struck or bowed object; banks of them make bells, bars, strings, drums. Reference: J.-M. Adrien, "The missing link: modal synthesis" (1991); M. Mathews & J. Smith, "Methods for synthesizing very high Q parametrically well behaved two pole filters" (SMAC 2003).
- types: `reso_t`
- `void reso_clear(reso_t *r)`
- `void reso_tune(reso_t *r, float freq_hz, float t60_s, float sample_rate)` — Frequency in Hz (clamped to 0.45 x SR) and decay time to -60 dB in seconds. Keeps the state.
- `void reso_strike(reso_t *r, float amp)` — Instant excitation: the mode starts ringing with amplitude amp (a sine starting at 0).
- `float reso_energy(const reso_t *r)` — Squared amplitude of the ringing (|z|^2).
- `void reso_ring(reso_t *r, float *restrict out, int n)` — Free ringing: adds n samples to out.
- `void reso_drive(reso_t *r, const float *restrict x, float g, float *restrict out, int n)` — Driven by g x[i]: adds n samples to out.
- `void reso_drive2(reso_t *r, const float *restrict x1, float g1, const float *restrict x2, float g2, float *restrict out, int n)` — Driven by two inputs (e.g. strike and bow): g1 x1[i] + g2 x2[i].

## `dsp/filter/scream.h`
2-pole low-pass in the spirit of late-70s semi-modular monosynth filters, with a screaming resonance: two one-pole TPT low-passes with a high-pass in the feedback path, resonance K up to self-oscillation, and a saturating feedback node that gives the aggressive, screaming character; optional 2x oversampling around the nonlinearity (halfband.h). Zero-delay feedback solved per sample. References: V. Zavalishin, "The Art of VA Filter Design" (TPT one-poles, ZDF feedback); W. Pirkle, "Designing Software Synthesizer Plugins in C++" (Korg 35 filter structure).
- types: `scream_t`
- `void scream_init(scream_t *f, float sample_rate)`
- `void scream_reset(scream_t *f)`
- `void scream_set_oversampling(scream_t *f, int factor)` — Runs the filter at 1, 2 or 4 times the sample rate (see ladder_set_oversampling).
- `void scream_set(scream_t *f, float cutoff_hz, float resonance, float drive)` — cutoff in Hz, resonance 0..1 (self-oscillation from about 0.91, bounded by the saturating node), drive 0..1 (saturation of the feedback node).
- `void scream_process(scream_t *f, const float *in, float *out, int n)` — in and out may be the same buffer.

## `dsp/filter/svf_tpt.h`
2-pole state variable filter in TPT/ZDF topology (trapezoidal, zero delay). Reference: V. Zavalishin, "The Art of VA Filter Design", ch. 4; A. Simper's "a1/a2/a3" form. Coefficients are linearly interpolated over the block: fast modulation without clicks or instability.
- types: `svf_mode_t`, `svf_t`
- `void svf_init(svf_t *s, float sample_rate)`
- `void svf_reset(svf_t *s)`
- `void svf_set_mode(svf_t *s, svf_mode_t mode)`
- `void svf_set(svf_t *s, float cutoff_hz, float q)` — Cutoff in Hz (clamped to 0.45*SR) and quality factor Q (0.707 = Butterworth).
- `void svf_process(svf_t *s, const float *in, float *out, int n)` — in and out may be the same. Normalized band-pass: unity gain at center.

## `dsp/filter/vfilter.h`
one filter slot of a voice, several characters behind one interface: 12 dB state-variable (low-pass, band-pass, high-pass, notch), vowel formant filter and 2-pole screaming low-pass with saturating feedback (oversampled 2x by default, or 1x / 4x). An engine keeps one vfilter_t per filter slot and per voice.
- types: `vf_type_t`, `vfilter_t`
- `void vfilter_init(vfilter_t *f, float sample_rate)`
- `void vfilter_reset(vfilter_t *f)`
- `void vfilter_set_oversampling(vfilter_t *f, int factor)` — Oversampling of the nonlinear characters (scream): 1, 2 (default) or 4; the others are linear.
- `void vfilter_set(vfilter_t *f, int type, float cutoff_hz, float q, float reso, float character)`
- `void vfilter_process(vfilter_t *f, const float *in, float *out, int n)`

## `dsp/env/adsr.h`
ADSR envelope with analog-style exponential segments (RC charge/discharge). Each segment aims at a target beyond its end point ("target ratio", cf. N. Redmon, EarLevel Engineering): the set time is exactly that of the full segment. A retrigger restarts from the current level (no click). Times clamped to 0.5 ms .. 30 s.
- types: `adsr_stage_t`, `adsr_t`
- constants: `ADSR_TIME_MIN` = 0.0005f, `ADSR_TIME_MAX` = 30.0f
- `void adsr_init(adsr_t *e, float sample_rate)`
- `void adsr_reset(adsr_t *e)`
- `void adsr_set(adsr_t *e, float attack_s, float decay_s, float sustain, float release_s)` — Times in seconds, sustain in [0, 1]. May be called at any time.
- `void adsr_gate(adsr_t *e, int on)`
- `void adsr_process(adsr_t *e, float *restrict out, int n)`
- `int adsr_active(const adsr_t *e)`

## `dsp/env/env_rl.h`
4-rate / 4-level envelope of the classic digital FM instruments: from level 4, go to levels 1, 2, 3 at rates 1, 2, 3, hold level 3 until key-off, then go to level 4 at rate 4. Levels are in a linear domain chosen by the caller (dB for amplitude: exponential-sounding segments; semitones for pitch); rates 0..99 map to the time of a full-scale sweep (env_rl_time). Stepped once per block. Reference: published documentation of the 1983 6-operator FM instrument (rate/level envelopes).
- types: `env_rl_t`
- `float env_rl_time(float rate)` — Seconds for a full-scale sweep at rate 0..99: 99 ~ 5 ms, 50 ~ 0.5 s, 30 ~ 3.5 s, 0 ~ 60 s.
- `void env_rl_step(env_rl_t *e, const float rates[4], const float levels[4], float rate_add, float full_scale, float dt)` — Advances by dt seconds. rate_add: keyboard rate scaling added to every rate; full_scale: the sweep that env_rl_time refers to (96 for dB).
- `void env_rl_gate(env_rl_t *e, int on)` — Key-on restarts from the current level (no click); key-off goes to the release stage.

## `dsp/env/mseg.h`
multi-segment envelope (loopable, any number of breakpoints): up to MSEG_POINTS points, each reached from the previous one in `time` (seconds, or beats when the caller advances it in beats) along a curve (-1..1: 0 = linear, > 0 = fast start then slow, < 0 = slow start then fast). A sustain point holds while the gate is on; loop points repeat a section either while the gate is on or forever. Retrigger and release start from the current value (no jump). Evaluated at control rate.
- types: `mseg_mode_t`, `mseg_shape_t`, `mseg_t`
- constants: `MSEG_POINTS` = 16
- `void mseg_reset(mseg_t *m, const mseg_shape_t *s)`
- `void mseg_gate(mseg_t *m, const mseg_shape_t *s, int on)` — idle at the first point's level
- `float mseg_advance(mseg_t *m, const mseg_shape_t *s, float dt)` — Advances by dt (seconds or beats) and returns the value. Bounded work whatever the times.
- `float mseg_progress(const mseg_t *m, const mseg_shape_t *s)` — Where it is along the shape's time axis, 0..1 of the whole shape (for a display), or -1 when idle or finished. Not for the audio path's decisions: a loop jumps back.

## `dsp/mod/lfo.h`
low-frequency oscillator evaluated at control rate (one value per block). Shapes: sine, triangle, saw, square, sample-and-hold. Bipolar output in [-1, 1]. No anti-aliasing needed: consumers interpolate the value over the block.
- types: `lfo_wave_t`, `lfo_t`
- `void lfo_init(lfo_t *l, float sample_rate, uint32_t seed)`
- `void lfo_reset(lfo_t *l, float phase)`
- `void lfo_set(lfo_t *l, float rate_hz, lfo_wave_t wave)`
- `float lfo_advance(lfo_t *l, int n)` — Advances by n samples and returns the value at the end of the step.

## `dsp/mod/modmatrix.h`
modulation matrix evaluated at control rate (CLAUDE.md, "Modulation"): slots {src, dst, amount, via}; each adds amount x src (x via, if any) to its destination. Sources and destinations are engine-defined indices; index 0 means "none" for both (via 0 = weight 1). The engine scales each destination into its own domain (semitones, octaves, normalized...).
- types: `mod_slot_t`
- `void modmatrix_eval(const mod_slot_t *slots, int n_slots, const float *src, int n_src, float *dst, int n_dst)` — src: values of the n_src sources (src[0] ignored); dst: n_dst outputs, overwritten (dst[0] unused).

## `dsp/mod/params.h`
parameter descriptors: the single source of truth for UIs, MIDI learn, presets, the generated catalog and AI agents. Each descriptor carries its range, default, unit, curve, the names of enumerated values and a one-line description of its effect on the sound. The only place where 0..1 normalization exists; the DSP itself works in physical units.
- types: `param_curve_t`, `param_desc_t`
- constants: `DSP_PARAM_TEXT` = 1
- data: `const char *const param_onoff_labels[]`, `const char *const param_oversample_labels[]`
- `float param_from_norm(const param_desc_t *d, float norm)` — Normalized value (clamped to 0..1) -> physical value.
- `float param_to_norm(const param_desc_t *d, float value)` — Physical value -> normalized value 0..1.
- `int param_find(const param_desc_t *table, int count, const char *name)` — Index of the parameter called name in a table, or -1.
- `int param_find_role(const param_desc_t *table, int count, const char *role)` — Index of the parameter with this role in a table, or -1 (first match).
- `int param_label(const param_desc_t *d, const char *label)` — Index of a label of an enumerated parameter, or -1.

## `dsp/mod/partmod.h`
parameter and modulation layer of a part, the same for every engine. Parameter changes made while notes sound (knobs, CCs, macros, routes) glide to their target with a 5 ms one-pole, for every engine; with nothing sounding they apply at once (patch loading stays exact). Modulation: 8 macros, 2 LFOs (free or tempo-synced), 2 MSEGs, MIDI sources (mod wheel, aftertouch, pitch bend, velocity, note, random per note) and 8 routes {source, destination, amount, via} onto any `realtime` parameter of the part's engine. Evaluated once per block: each modulated parameter gets base + sum of its routes (normalized domain, clamped) through the engine's set_param; when a route goes away the base value is restored. One value per part (all voices).
- types: `partmod_t`
- constants: `PM_MACROS` = 8, `PM_LFOS` = 2, `PM_MSEGS` = 2, `PM_ROUTES` = 8, `PM_ENGINE_PARAMS` = 256, `PM_SMOOTH_S` = 0.005f, `PM_VBASE`, `PM_COUNT`, `PM_WAVE_FOURIER` = 5, `PM_WAVE_WIENER` = 6
- data: `const param_desc_t partmod_params[PM_COUNT]`
- `void partmod_init(partmod_t *m, float sample_rate, uint32_t seed)`
- `void partmod_engine(partmod_t *m, const engine_ops_t *ops)` — New engine: base values back to the engine's defaults, nothing modulated.
- `void partmod_set(partmod_t *m, int index, float norm)` — Modulation parameter index (0..PM_COUNT-1), normalized value.
- `int partmod_macro_cc(const partmod_t *m, int cc)` — The macro (0..7) a CC turns on this part, or -1.
- `void partmod_global_targets(const partmod_t *m, float *val, uint8_t *set)` — Adds this part's macro targets on synth-level parameters (master, effects) into val[id - SYNTH_PARAM_GLOBAL] (normalized; set[i] = 1 once a target is seen, the first target's `from` starting the sum).
- `int partmod_base(partmod_t *m, const engine_ops_t *ops, int id, float norm, int sounding)` — Base value of an engine parameter set by the user or MIDI. Returns 1 if the layer takes care of it (it glides because notes sound, or it is modulated), 0 if the caller must give it to the engine now.
- `void partmod_note_on(partmod_t *m, int note, float velocity)`
- `void partmod_note_off(partmod_t *m)`
- `void partmod_all_notes_off(partmod_t *m)`
- `void partmod_tuning(partmod_t *m, const float *offsets, int root)` — Microtuning (12 offsets in semitones from root, NULL = equal temperament) and MPE, set by the synth.
- `void partmod_mpe(partmod_t *m, int on, float bend_range)`
- `void partmod_midi_source(partmod_t *m, int src, float v)`
- `void partmod_block(partmod_t *m, const tempo_t *t, int n, const engine_ops_t *ops, void *eng)` — Once per block, before the engine renders: sources, routes, engine parameters.

## `dsp/mod/tempo.h`
tempo and beat position, from an internal BPM or from MIDI clock (24 ticks per quarter note, start / continue / stop). The clock period is smoothed (one-pole over the tick intervals, outliers rejected) so LFOs and delays do not jitter; the beat position locks to the tick count. Musical divisions shared by every tempo-synced element (delay, LFOs, MSEGs). Reference: MIDI 1.0 specification, timing clock.
- types: `tempo_t`
- constants: `TEMPO_DIV_COUNT` = 17
- data: `const char *const tempo_div_labels[TEMPO_DIV_COUNT + 1]`, `const float tempo_div_beats[TEMPO_DIV_COUNT]`
- `void tempo_init(tempo_t *t, float sample_rate, float bpm)`
- `void tempo_set_bpm(tempo_t *t, float bpm)` — Internal tempo (used when not following the clock, or before the clock has a period).
- `void tempo_set_external(tempo_t *t, int on)`
- `void tempo_clock(tempo_t *t, uint32_t time)` — MIDI real-time messages, with their time in samples.
- `void tempo_start(tempo_t *t)`
- `void tempo_continue(tempo_t *t)` — 0xFA: back to beat 0
- `void tempo_stop(tempo_t *t)` — 0xFB
- `void tempo_advance(tempo_t *t, int n)` — Advances by n samples (call once per block).
- `float tempo_div_seconds(const tempo_t *t, int div)` — Seconds of division div (> 0) at the current tempo.

## `dsp/voice/analog.h`
the imperfections of an analog oscillator, one state per oscillator: a static offset drawn once (the tolerance of its parts), a slow Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift (standard deviation and time constant) and a light jitter (white frequency noise at block rate, so the phase wanders as a Wiener process: irregular beats). Output in cents, once per block. OU update: x += -a x + sqrt(2 a) w, w of unit variance, a = dt / tau.
- types: `analog_cfg_t`, `analog_t`
- `void analog_cfg(analog_cfg_t *c, float tolerance, float sd, float tau, float jitter, float dt)` — dt = block duration (s); tolerance and sd in cents, tau in seconds (> 0), jitter in cents
- `void analog_init(analog_t *s, uint32_t seed)` — a new oscillator: its offset and a start already in the walk's spread (no settling from zero)
- `float analog_next(analog_t *s, const analog_cfg_t *c)` — cents to add to the oscillator's pitch this block

## `dsp/voice/voice.h`
the few steps every engine voice shares: constant-power pan, glide coefficient, envelope x gain ramp, and the voice output (steal fade, NaN guard, pan into the stereo bus). Engines get it through engine.h; keeping these in one place keeps every voice tail identical.
- `void voice_pan(float pos, float *pan_l, float *pan_r)` — Constant-power pan: pos -1 (left) .. +1 (right) -> gains for L and R (quarter of a sine cycle).
- `float voice_glide_coef(float time_s, int n, float sample_rate)` — One-pole glide: fraction of the remaining distance covered in n samples for a glide time in seconds (time constant = time / 3, i.e. ~95 % of the way after `time`).
- `float voice_glide_arrive_coef(float time_s, int n, float sample_rate)` — One-pole glide that arrives: the time constant is time / 4.6, so the pitch is within 1 % of the interval after `time` (an RC lag set by its arrival, as a player hears it) instead of still trailing behind.
- `void dsp_ramp_env_mul(float *restrict x, const float *restrict env, float g0, float g1, int n)` — x[i] *= env[i] * g, g ramping linearly from g0 (excluded) to g1 (reached on the last sample).
- `void voice_vmod_apply(vpoly_t *p, int vi, float *x, int n, float *pan_from, float *pan_to)` — Per-voice level (ramped over the block) of voice vi, and its pan offset at the start and at the end of the block (balance on top of the voice's own pan); nothing when no per-voice modulation is configured (bit-exact w...
- `void voice_pan_offset(float d, float pan_l, float pan_r, float *l, float *r)` — Gains of a pan offset d (-1..1) applied to a voice's own pan: the far side is attenuated.
- `void voice_pan_out(float *x, int n, float pan_l, float pan_r, float *L, float *R, uint32_t *nan_count)` — NaN guard then pan of a mono voice block into the stereo bus (L, R accumulate).
- `void voice_vmod_out(vpoly_t *p, int vi, float *x, int n, float pan_l, float pan_r, float *L, float *R, uint32_t *nan_count)` — Per-voice modulation of level and pan of voice vi, NaN guard, then pan into the stereo bus.
- `void voice_out(vpoly_t *p, int vi, float *x, int n, float pan_l, float pan_r, float *L, float *R, uint32_t *nan_count)` — Output of voice vi: applies its steal fade (vpoly), then voice_vmod_out.

## `dsp/voice/voice_alloc.h`
polyphonic voice allocation, engine independent. Same note already active: retrigger it. Otherwise a free voice; otherwise steal, by priority: oldest released voice, then oldest pedal-sustained voice, then the quietest. The fade-out (2 to 5 ms) before reuse is done by the engine (*steal = 1).
- types: `valloc_slot_t`, `valloc_t`
- constants: `VALLOC_MAX` = 16
- `void valloc_init(valloc_t *a, int n_voices)`
- `int valloc_note_on(valloc_t *a, int note, const float *levels, int *steal)` — levels[v]: current amplitude of each voice (may be NULL). Returns the chosen voice; *steal = 1 if it was playing another note (fade needed).
- `int valloc_note_off(valloc_t *a, int note)` — Returns the voice to release, or -1 (unknown note or held by the pedal).
- `int valloc_set_sustain(valloc_t *a, int on, int *out)` — Sustain pedal. On release, writes the voices to release into out[]; returns their count.
- `int valloc_release_all(valloc_t *a, int *out)` — Releases all held notes; writes the voices into out[], returns their count.
- `void valloc_voice_done(valloc_t *a, int v)` — Call when the voice has finished sounding (envelope idle).

## `dsp/voice/voicemod.h`
per-voice modulation, the same for every engine: each voice has its own MSEG and LFO, its note, velocity and random value, and its MPE expression (per-note pitch bend, pressure, slide); 4 routes send them to five voice destinations every engine understands: pitch (semitones), level (dB), pan, brightness (octaves of the engine's main brightness control) and timbre (-1..1 on the engine's main timbre control). Microtuning is a per-voice pitch offset too. Lives in vpoly; engines read vpoly_vmod().
- types: `voicemod_cfg_t`, `voicemod_t`
- constants: `VM_ROUTES` = 4, `VM_PITCH_RANGE` = 12.0f, `VM_LEVEL_RANGE` = 24.0f, `VM_BRIGHT_RANGE` = 4.0f, `VM_WIENER_N` = 32
- `void voicemod_wiener_build(float *w, uint32_t seed)`
- `float voicemod_wiener(const float *w, float ph)`
- `float voicemod_fourier(const float *c, float ph)`
- `void voicemod_init(voicemod_t *m, uint32_t seed)`
- `void voicemod_start(voicemod_t *m, const voicemod_cfg_t *c, int note, float velocity, int hard)`
- `void voicemod_note(voicemod_t *m, const voicemod_cfg_t *c, int note)`
- `void voicemod_release(voicemod_t *m, const voicemod_cfg_t *c)` — legato: new note, envelope goes on
- `void voicemod_block(voicemod_t *m, const voicemod_cfg_t *c)` — Once per block: updates out[] (all zero when nothing is configured).
- `int voicemod_cfg_active(const voicemod_cfg_t *c)` — 1 if this configuration can move anything at all (routes, tuning, MPE).

## `dsp/voice/vpoly.h`
engine-independent polyphony manager: voice allocation (voice_alloc), click-free voice stealing (3 ms fade-out, then the new note starts), sustain pedal, all-notes/sound-off and voice lifetime, and monophonic play (mono / legato, last-note priority, return to the previous held note). An engine keeps only its DSP state per voice and provides the callbacks below. Engine side, per block: for each voice v with vpoly_active(p, v): render the voice into x[], multiply by vpoly_fade(p, v, g, n) vpoly_end_block(p, v, still_sounding)
- types: `vpoly_ops_t`, `vpoly_mode_t`, `vpoly_voice_t`, `vpoly_t`, `vpoly_priority_t`
- constants: `VPOLY_HELD_MAX` = 16
- `void vpoly_init(vpoly_t *p, int n_voices, float sample_rate, const vpoly_ops_t *ops, void *eng)`
- `void vpoly_set_vmod(vpoly_t *p, const voicemod_cfg_t *cfg)` — Per-voice modulation configuration (owned by the part), or NULL.
- `const float *vpoly_vmod(vpoly_t *p, int v)` — Per-voice modulation of voice v for this block: VM_PITCH (st), VM_LEVEL (dB), VM_PAN, VM_BRIGHT (oct), VM_TIMBRE.
- `void vpoly_expression(vpoly_t *p, int note, int what, float value)` — MPE expression of the voice(s) playing `note`: what = VM_SRC_PRESSURE, VM_SRC_SLIDE (0..1) or -1 = bend (-1..1).
- `void vpoly_note_on(vpoly_t *p, int note, float velocity)`
- `void vpoly_note_off(vpoly_t *p, int note)`
- `void vpoly_sustain(vpoly_t *p, int on)`
- `void vpoly_all_notes_off(vpoly_t *p)`
- `void vpoly_all_sound_off(vpoly_t *p)`
- `int vpoly_active_count(const vpoly_t *p)`
- `void vpoly_set_mode(vpoly_t *p, vpoly_mode_t mode)`
- `void vpoly_set_priority(vpoly_t *p, vpoly_priority_t priority)`
- `int vpoly_overlap(const vpoly_t *p)` — 1 if the current note was reached while another key was held (legato playing): engines use it to decide whether to glide. Valid inside the start/legato callbacks.
- `int vpoly_active(const vpoly_t *p, int v)`
- `int vpoly_note(const vpoly_t *p, int v)`
- `int vpoly_fade(vpoly_t *p, int v, float *gain, int n)` — Fills gain[0..n) with the steal fade of voice v (all 1 when not stealing). Returns 0 when the gains are all 1, so the caller may skip the multiplication.
- `void vpoly_end_block(vpoly_t *p, int v, int sounding)` — End of the block for voice v: after a completed fade, starts the pending note (or frees the voice); otherwise frees the voice when sounding == 0 (its envelope reached silence).

## `dsp/fx/chorus.h`
analog-style chorus/ensemble on short modulated delay lines (mono in, stereo out). Modes: I and II = two lines driven by one triangle LFO in antiphase (L/R), slow/deeper vs faster, in the manner of classic BBD chorus units; I+II = both LFOs summed; ENSEMBLE = three lines whose delays follow a slow and a fast sine 120 degrees apart (string-machine ensemble). The wet path is low-passed (~9 kHz, BBD bandwidth). Reference: Zolzer (ed.), DAFX, "Chorus".
- types: `chorus_mode_t`, `chorus_t`
- `void chorus_init(chorus_t *c, float sample_rate)`
- `void chorus_reset(chorus_t *c)`
- `void chorus_set(chorus_t *c, chorus_mode_t mode, float mix)` — mix: wet amount 0..1 added to the dry signal (dry stays at unity).
- `void chorus_process(chorus_t *c, const float *inL, const float *inR, float *outL, float *outR, int n)` — outL/outR may alias inL/inR.

## `dsp/fx/delay.h`
stereo "tape" echo: fractional delay lines read with 4-point Hermite interpolation, delay-time changes glide like a tape speed change, wow (slow) and flutter (fast) modulation, and a feedback path with low-pass/high-pass "tone" and soft saturation, so repeats get darker and grainier. Stereo or ping-pong. Wet-only output. Memory supplied by the caller. References: U. Zolzer (ed.), DAFX, ch. "Delays" and "Modulation"; Hermite interpolation after Laakso et al., "Splitting the unit delay" (IEEE SPM 1996).
- types: `delay_t`
- `size_t delay_mem_floats(float sample_rate, float max_time_s)` — Floats of memory needed for a maximum delay time (both channels).
- `void delay_init(delay_t *d, float sample_rate, float max_time_s, float *mem)`
- `void delay_reset(delay_t *d)`
- `void delay_set(delay_t *d, float time_s, float ratio_r, float feedback, float tone_hz, float drive, float wow, int pingpong)` — time_s: left delay; right = time_s * ratio_r (stereo mode) or time_s (ping-pong). feedback 0..0.98, tone_hz: feedback low-pass cutoff (repeats darker below), drive 0..1 saturation, wow 0..1 (tape wobble amount), pingp...
- `void delay_snap(delay_t *d)` — Jump to the target delay time without the tape glide (use when the effect starts from idle).
- `void delay_process(delay_t *d, const float *inL, const float *inR, float *outL, float *outR, int n)` — Mono-compatible stereo input, wet stereo output (outL/outR overwritten; may alias inL/inR).

## `dsp/fx/fxbus.h`
the synth's effect bus: chorus (insert) -> tape delay -> plate reverb (both parallel, wet added to the dry signal), with its parameter descriptors. Delay and reverb memory comes from a caller-provided arena; if the arena is too small the reverb size and maximum delay time shrink. An effect whose mix stays at 0 is fed silence, then stops being computed after its tail (CPU).
- types: `fxbus_t`
- data: `const param_desc_t fxbus_params[FXB_P_COUNT]`
- `size_t fxbus_mem_floats(float sample_rate, float max_delay_s, float reverb_size)` — Arena size for a delay of max_delay_s and a reverb of the given size at this sample rate.
- `void fxbus_init(fxbus_t *f, float sample_rate, float *mem, size_t mem_floats, float max_delay_s, float reverb_size)` — mem/mem_floats: arena for delay + reverb (may be NULL/0: then only the chorus is available).
- `void fxbus_set_param(fxbus_t *f, int id, float norm)`
- `void fxbus_process(fxbus_t *f, float *L, float *R, int n)` — Processes one block in place (n <= SYNTH_BLOCK).

## `dsp/fx/reverb.h`
plate reverb after J. Dattorro, "Effect Design Part 1: Reverberator and Other Filters" (JAES 45(9), 1997): predelay, input bandwidth filter, 4 input diffusers, figure-of-eight tank with two modulated allpasses and damping. Mono in, stereo out (wet only). Delays scaled from the paper's 29761 Hz to the actual rate. Memory is provided by the caller (no allocation).
- types: `reverb_line_t`, `reverb_t`
- constants: `REVERB_MAX_PREDELAY_S` = 0.25f
- `size_t reverb_mem_floats(float sample_rate, float max_size)` — Floats of memory needed for a sample rate and maximum size.
- `void reverb_init(reverb_t *r, float sample_rate, float size, float *mem)` — mem must hold reverb_mem_floats(sample_rate, size) floats. size in 0.5..REVERB_MAX_SIZE.
- `void reverb_reset(reverb_t *r)`
- `void reverb_set(reverb_t *r, float decay, float damping_hz, float predelay_s)` — decay 0..0.99 (tail length), damping_hz: high-frequency loss in the tank (darker when lower), predelay_s: 0..0.25 s.
- `void reverb_set_freeze(reverb_t *r, int on)` — Freeze: the tank becomes (almost) lossless and the input is closed, so the current tail holds indefinitely; turning it off lets the tail decay normally. Transitions are smoothed (~50 ms).
- `void reverb_process(reverb_t *r, const float *in, float *outL, float *outR, int n)` — Mono input, wet stereo output (outL/outR are overwritten).

## `dsp/engines/acid.h`
monophonic acid bass engine, in the spirit of the early-80s transistor bass line machine: one saw/square oscillator, 18 dB ladder low-pass (2x oversampled) with high resonance, a decaying filter envelope, accent (velocity >= 96: louder, shorter and brighter envelope, plus an "accent sweep" that builds up over consecutive accents) and slide (overlapping notes glide without retriggering). Behaviour reconstructed from published circuit descriptions; no code reused.
- types: `acid_t`
- data: `const param_desc_t acid_params[ACID_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t acid_engine`

## `dsp/engines/coupled.h`
coupled-oscillator engine: each note is a network of partials, each a Stuart-Landau oscillator (normal form of the Hopf bifurcation). Its modulus saturates by itself; the modulus bends its pitch (pitch_by_level: louder = flatter); the phase relations with its neighbours, compared on the fundamental (n:m harmonic coupling), feed or starve its modulus (amp_coupling: > 0 cooperation, < 0 competition) and pull its pitch (phase_coupling: locking onto the harmonic series). Random detune and a slow random drift keep the network moving; freeze switches to diffusive coupling, where detuned partials kill each other (amplitude death). Couplings are integrated once per block; partial phases and levels are interpolated per sample. References: Y. Kuramoto, "Chemical Oscillations, Waves, and Turbulence" (1984); A. Pikovsky, M. Rosenblum, J. Kurths, "Synchronization" (2001); the experiments in tools/experiments/.
- types: `coupled_voice_t`, `coupled_t`
- constants: `CPL_VOICES` = 8, `CPL_PARTIALS` = 24
- data: `const param_desc_t coupled_params[CPL_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t coupled_engine`

## `dsp/engines/drone.h`
drone engine: each note is a whole drone that never repeats. Four layers: partials (harmonic sines, glassy and slightly stretched when cold, with two beating twins), a body (two detuned saws in a low-pass, faded in as it warms up), air (noise in two band-passes on the note's harmonics) and sparkles (rare pings of a high harmonic). Every partial's level, pitch and place wander on smoothed random walks (no cycle to hear), and the two slow LFOs of a note have periods in the golden ratio. Seven macros move it all: temperature (glacial .. warm), density, motion, depth, brightness, sparkle, width. Envelopes up to 3 minutes. References: the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process for the walks; additive synthesis of harmonic series (J.-C. Risset).
- types: `drone_walk_t`, `drone_voice_t`, `drone_t`
- constants: `DRN_VOICES` = 8, `DRN_PARTIALS` = 12
- data: `const param_desc_t drone_params[DRN_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t drone_engine`

## `dsp/engines/drums.h`
drum machine engine: 12 instruments on General-MIDI note numbers, two kits: "analog" (in the spirit of the classic early-80s analog machines: resonant sine kick with a long boom, two-tone + noise snare, 6 detuned square "metal" oscillators for hats/cymbal, multi-burst clap, cowbell from two squares), "hybrid" (mid-80s analog/sample hybrids: punchy waveshaped kick with a deep pitch sweep and click, brighter snappy snare, grittier 6-bit-quantized metal) and "glitch" (digital microsound: gated sub sine pulses, single-sample clicks, pure high beeps, white and sample-rate-reduced data noise, ring-modulated modem chirps, on precise grids). Behaviour reconstructed from published circuit analyses and listening; no code or samples reused. Velocity acts as accent. The closed hat chokes the open hat.
- types: `drum_voice_t`, `drums_t`
- constants: `DRUMS_VOICES` = 16, `DRUMS_P_COUNT`
- data: `const param_desc_t drums_params[DRUMS_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t drums_engine`, `const char *const drums_instrument_names[DR_COUNT]`, `const uint8_t drums_instrument_notes[DR_COUNT]`
- `int drums_instrument_for_note(int note)` — Instrument for a MIDI note (GM drum map), or -1.

## `dsp/engines/engine.h`
the interface every synthesis engine implements, and the engine registry. synth.c only talks to engines through this table: adding an engine = one source file exporting an engine_ops_t + one line in registry.c + one value in synth_engine_t. Notes, sustain and all-notes/sound-off go through the engine's shared polyphony manager (vpoly).
- types: `engine_cc_t`, `engine_note_t`, `engine_stage_t`, `engine_ops_t`
- data: `const engine_ops_t *const engine_registry[SYNTH_ENGINE_COUNT]`
- `const engine_ops_t *engine_find(const char *name)` — Engine by name, or NULL.
- `int engine_id(const engine_ops_t *e)` — Its synth_engine_t id, or -1.

## `dsp/engines/fm6.h`
6-operator phase-modulation synthesizer in the spirit of the 1983 digital FM classic: 32 algorithms, 4-rate/4-level envelopes working in dB, output levels 0..99, ratio/fixed frequency with fine and detune, keyboard level and rate scaling, velocity sensitivity, self feedback averaged over 2 samples, pitch envelope, LFO (6 shapes, delay, pitch/amp modulation sensitivities), transpose, oscillator key sync. Parameters use the instrument's native 0..99 scales so voices imported from its documented sysex format map 1:1 (host/fm6_sysex.c). Behaviour reconstructed from public documentation (J. Chowning 1973 for FM; the instrument's published algorithm chart and data format).
- types: `fm6_voice_t`, `fm6_t`, `fm6_algorithm_t`
- constants: `FM6_VOICES` = 16, `FM6_OPS` = 6
- data: `const param_desc_t fm6_params[FM6_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t fm6_engine`, `const fm6_algorithm_t fm6_algorithms[32]`

## `dsp/engines/modal.h`
modal synthesis engine: each voice is a bank of up to 32 damped resonators (modes) excited by a mallet strike (raised-cosine pulse + noise burst) and/or a continuous "bow" (filtered noise). Mode frequency ratios come from physical models (ideal string, stiff string, free bar, tuned marimba bar, church bell, circular membrane, bowl, closed tube); decay, damping of high modes, brightness and strike position shape the timbre. References: J.-M. Adrien, "The missing link: modal synthesis" (1991); P. Cook, "Real Sound Synthesis for Interactive Applications" (2002); N. Fletcher & T. Rossing, "The Physics of Musical Instruments" (mode ratios, stiff-string inharmonicity f_k = k f0 sqrt(1 + B k^2)); G. Weinreich, "Coupled piano strings" (JASA 1977) for the unison beating and double decay.
- types: `modal_voice_t`, `modal_t`
- constants: `MODAL_MODES` = 32
- data: `const param_desc_t modal_params[MODAL_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t modal_engine`

## `dsp/engines/mono.h`
classic monophonic synthesizer modelled on the early-70s portable modular-derived monosynth and its current reissue, panel by panel from the public owner's manual: 3 free-running oscillators (6 waveforms, footage LO and 32'..2', reverse saw on osc 3, osc 3 usable as a modulation source with keyboard control off), white or pink noise, a mixer that overloads the filter and can take the instrument's own output back in (the external input left unplugged), a 24 dB transistor-ladder filter whose emphasis thins the bass and self-oscillates, keyboard control of the filter, attack/decay/sustain contours with the "decay as release" switch, the modulation mix (osc 3 or filter contour against noise or the added LFO) sent by the wheel to the oscillators and the filter, glide, single or multiple triggering, low / last / high note priority. Behaviour reconstructed from the documentation; no code reused.
- types: `mono_t`
- data: `const param_desc_t mono_params[MONO_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t mono_engine`

## `dsp/engines/poly.h`
classic programmable polysynth in the spirit of the late-70s 5-voice instrument: per voice osc A (saw + pulse, hard-synced to B on demand) and osc B (saw + triangle + pulse, low-frequency mode, keytrack switch), noise, 24 dB ladder, filter and amp ADSR, and POLY-MOD: filter envelope and osc B modulate osc A frequency and pulse width (osc B at audio rate) and the cutoff. Global LFO with initial amount + mod wheel, glide, unison, analog "slop". Behaviour reconstructed from public documentation; no code reused.
- types: `poly_voice_t`, `poly_t`
- constants: `POLY_VOICES` = 8
- data: `const param_desc_t poly_params[POLY_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t poly_engine`

## `dsp/engines/registry.h`
storage able to hold the state of any engine (one per part). Included by synth.c only; everything else uses engine.h.
- types: `engine_state_t`

## `dsp/engines/sampler.h`
a drum sampler: plays the samples of a kit (core/kit.h, given by synth_part_kit), one per MIDI note. The first 16 samples of the kit are pads with their own settings: speed (pitch), start and end points, reverse, loop, decay, level, pan, low-pass cutoff and choke group (a closed hi-hat stops the open one); further samples play with the default settings. One-shot: a pad plays to its end whatever the note-off, unless it loops (it then stops at the note-off, after the release). Band-limited playback (osc/splay.h).
- types: `sampler_stage_t`, `sampler_voice_t`, `sampler_sample_t`, `sampler_t`
- constants: `SAMPLER_VOICES` = 12, `SAMPLER_PADS` = 16, `SAMPLER_P_COUNT`
- data: `const param_desc_t sampler_params[SAMPLER_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t sampler_engine`

## `dsp/engines/selfosc.h`
self-oscillating engine: each voice is a Van der Pol / Duffing oscillator forced by the note (dsp/osc/selfosc.h): drive morphs a sine into a relaxation wave, stiffness makes the pitch follow the amplitude, entrain locks it to the note (or lets it beat against it when detuned), velocity can add drive. Then a filter slot (vfilter: lp/bp/hp/notch, formant, scream; or a feedback comb, dsp/filter/comb) and an amp envelope.
- types: `so_voice_t`, `selfosc_engine_t`
- constants: `SO_VOICES` = 8
- data: `const param_desc_t selfosc_params[SO_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t selfosc_engine`

## `dsp/engines/sine.h`
reference engine (M0): polyphonic sine with one ADSR. Used to validate the full chain (MIDI, voices, master) and tuning accuracy.
- types: `sine_voice_t`, `sine_engine_t`
- constants: `SINE_VOICES` = 8
- data: `const param_desc_t sine_params[SINE_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t sine_engine`

## `dsp/engines/va.h`
"va" subtractive engine (M1, inspired by a 2-oscillator virtual analog). Per voice: 2 polyBLEP oscillators (or supersaws) + noise, two filter slots in series or parallel (state-variable, formant, screaming 2-pole), amp and filter ADSR, pitch envelope, three desynchronized detune LFOs, analog imperfections (tolerance, drift, jitter) per oscillator. Global: 1 LFO (pitch, cutoff, PWM), mod wheel -> vibrato, pitch bend; poly, mono or legato with glide.
- types: `va_voice_t`, `va_t`
- constants: `VA_VOICES` = 8, `VA_WAVE_SUPERSAW` = 4
- data: `const param_desc_t va_params[VA_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t va_engine`

## `dsp/engines/wt.h`
wavetable synthesizer in the spirit of modern wavetable instruments: two wavetable oscillators (9 generated tables, position morphing, unison up to 8, warps: sync, bend, mirror, FM from B, ring by B; osc B's FM/ring source is the sub), sine sub one octave down, noise, one filter (12 dB state-variable LP/BP/HP/notch or 24 dB ladder with drive), amp envelope, a modulation envelope, two per-voice LFOs and a 6-slot modulation matrix (dsp/mod/modmatrix.h). Mono, legato and glide. No code from any product.
- types: `wt_voice_t`, `wt_t`
- constants: `WT_VOICES` = 8, `WT_SLOTS` = 6
- data: `const param_desc_t wt_params[WT_P_COUNT]`, `const engine_ops_t wt_engine`

## `dsp/global_params.h`
descriptors of the global parameters (SYNTH_PARAM_GLOBAL and above): master level and effect bus. For hosts, catalogs and agents; the audio path does not need it.
- types: `synth_cc_doc_t`
- constants: `SYNTH_MOD_COUNT`
- data: `const synth_cc_doc_t synth_midi_cc[]`, `const int synth_midi_cc_count`, `const engine_stage_t synth_fx_stages[]`, `const int synth_fx_stage_count`, `const int synth_mod_count`
- `const param_desc_t *synth_global_param(int index)` — Descriptor of global parameter SYNTH_PARAM_GLOBAL + index, or NULL.
- `const param_desc_t *synth_part_param_info(int index)` — Descriptor of part parameter SYNTH_PART_PARAM + index, or NULL.
- `const param_desc_t *synth_mod_param_info(int index)`

## `dsp/synth_debug.h`
diagnostics of an instance, for tests and for a board's status screen; not part of the public API (dsp/synth.h), and free to change.
- `void *synth_debug_engine_state(synth_t *s, int part)` — The state of the engine of a part (engines/registry.h: engine_state_t), or NULL if the part is off. Tests use it to inject a fault.
- `uint32_t synth_debug_nan_count(const synth_t *s)` — How many times a part's or the effects' output was not finite (NaN or Inf) and was reset since synth_init.

## `dsp/synth_probe.h`
read-only views of an instance's state for displays (the web page, the board's screen): where the modulation envelopes are. Nothing here changes the sound; call it from the interface thread between renders (the value can be one block old). Kept apart from synth.h, the control API.
- `float synth_probe_mseg(const synth_t *s, int part, int which)` — Position of an envelope along its shape, 0..1, or -1 when it is not running. which: 0 and 1 = the part's envelopes (MSEG 1 and 2), 2 = the per-note envelope of the most recent note still running.

## `midi/link.h`
the board link: how a host (the Mac, later the Pi hub) drives a synth board over Ethernet with UDP datagrams. One datagram = a 12-byte header + one message: MIDI, parameter values, a preset, the choice of a built-in preset, or a chunk of a large transfer (a sample kit). Specified in docs/link.md. Encoding and decoding only (no sockets, no allocation, little-endian fields), shared by the board and the host tools; the transport is udpip.h on the board and BSD sockets on the host.
- types: `link_type_t`, `link_status_t`, `link_kind_t`, `link_header_t`, `link_hello_t`, `link_param_t`, `link_preset_t`, `link_xfer_t`, `link_rx_t`
- constants: `LINK_VERSION` = 1u, `LINK_HEADER` = 12, `LINK_MAX_PAYLOAD`
- `void link_put_header(uint8_t *out, const link_header_t *h)` — Writes the header into out (LINK_HEADER bytes).
- `int link_get_header(const uint8_t *in, int len, link_header_t *h)` — Reads a datagram's header; returns the payload length, or -1 if it is not a link datagram of this version.
- `int link_for_me(uint32_t dest, uint32_t id)` — 1 if a datagram with this destination is for the board of this id.
- `uint32_t link_board_id(const uint8_t *uid, int len)` — Board id: FNV-1a of the MCU's unique id (never 0).
- `int link_encode_hello(uint8_t *out, const link_header_t *h, const link_hello_t *m)` — Encoders: write the payload after the header into out (LINK_MAX_DATAGRAM bytes), return the datagram's length, or -1 if it does not fit.
- `int link_encode_ack(uint8_t *out, const link_header_t *h, uint32_t seq, uint8_t status)`
- `int link_encode_midi(uint8_t *out, const link_header_t *h, const uint8_t *bytes, int len)`
- `int link_encode_param(uint8_t *out, const link_header_t *h, uint32_t catalog, const link_param_t *p, int count)`
- `int link_encode_select(uint8_t *out, const link_header_t *h, const char *name)`
- `int link_encode_preset(uint8_t *out, const link_header_t *h, const link_preset_t *m)`
- `int link_encode_xfer_begin(uint8_t *out, const link_header_t *h, const link_xfer_t *m)`
- `int link_encode_xfer_data(uint8_t *out, const link_header_t *h, uint32_t xfer, uint32_t offset, const uint8_t *data, int len)`
- `int link_encode_xfer_ack(uint8_t *out, const link_header_t *h, uint32_t xfer, uint32_t next, uint8_t status)`
- `int link_decode_hello(const uint8_t *p, int len, link_hello_t *m)` — Decoders: read a payload (after link_get_header); return 0, or -1 if malformed.
- `int link_decode_ack(const uint8_t *p, int len, uint32_t *seq, uint8_t *status)`
- `int link_decode_param(const uint8_t *p, int len, uint32_t *catalog, link_param_t *out, int max, int *count)`
- `int link_decode_select(const uint8_t *p, int len, char name[LINK_NAME])`
- `int link_decode_preset(const uint8_t *p, int len, link_preset_t *m)`
- `int link_decode_xfer_begin(const uint8_t *p, int len, link_xfer_t *m)`
- `int link_decode_xfer_data(const uint8_t *p, int len, uint32_t *xfer, uint32_t *offset, const uint8_t **data, int *n)`
- `int link_decode_xfer_ack(const uint8_t *p, int len, uint32_t *xfer, uint32_t *next, uint8_t *status)`
- `int link_midi_next(const uint8_t *p, int len, int *pos)` — Splits the payload of a LINK_MIDI message: returns the length of the message at p[*pos] and advances *pos, 0 at the end, -1 if malformed (a data byte where a status is expected, or a message cut short). Channel messag...
- `uint32_t link_crc32(uint32_t crc, const uint8_t *data, size_t n)` — CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, reflected, as zlib's crc32): crc = link_crc32(0, data, n), chainable.
- `void link_rx_init(link_rx_t *r, uint8_t *mem, uint32_t capacity)`
- `uint8_t link_rx_begin(link_rx_t *r, const link_xfer_t *x)` — A BEGIN: starts over (even for the same id). Returns the status to acknowledge.
- `uint8_t link_rx_data(link_rx_t *r, uint32_t xfer, uint32_t offset, const uint8_t *data, int n)` — A DATA chunk. Returns the status to acknowledge (with r->next); LINK_OK once, when the last byte arrives and the CRC matches.

## `midi/linkq.h`
a lock-free single-producer, single-consumer queue of small events (MIDI messages and parameter values), for the network core of a board to hand events to its audio core through shared memory (on the H745: the M4 pushes from its Ethernet interrupt, the M7 pops at the start of each audio buffer). Each index has one writer; a barrier orders the event before the index that publishes it (Lamport's queue).
- types: `linkq_kind_t`, `linkq_event_t`, `linkq_t`
- constants: `LINKQ_LEN` = 256u
- `void linkq_barrier(void)`
- `void linkq_init(linkq_t *q)` — Both indexes to 0 (before either core uses the queue).
- `int linkq_push(linkq_t *q, const linkq_event_t *e)` — Producer: returns 1, or 0 if the queue is full (the event is counted in lost).
- `int linkq_pop(linkq_t *q, linkq_event_t *e)` — Consumer: returns 1 with the oldest event in e, or 0 if the queue is empty.

## `midi/midi.h`
platform-independent MIDI parsing: 4-byte USB-MIDI 1.0 packets (USB Device Class for MIDI Devices 1.0 specification, sec. 4) and DIN byte stream with running status. SysEx is ignored for now.
- types: `midi_msg_t`, `midi_din_t`
- `int midi_usb_decode(const uint8_t pkt[4], midi_msg_t *out)` — Decodes a USB-MIDI packet. Returns 1 if out holds a message, 0 otherwise (CIN 0/1, SysEx, invalid).
- `void midi_din_init(midi_din_t *p)`
- `int midi_din_feed(midi_din_t *p, uint8_t byte, midi_msg_t *out)` — Feeds one byte; returns 1 when a complete message is available in out. Real-time messages (F8..FF) are returned immediately without disturbing the running status.
- `int midi_channel_data_len(uint8_t status)` — Number of data bytes of a channel message (0x80..0xEF), or -1.

## `midi/udpip.h`
the smallest IPv4 stack a synth board needs: Ethernet II frames in and out, ARP replies, ICMP echo (ping), and UDP on one port, unicast, broadcast or one multicast group. No TCP, no fragments, no routing, no ARP table: a reply goes back to the MAC and IP the request came from. Static memory only; the driver gives it received frames and sends the frames it builds. RFC 791 (IPv4), 826 (ARP), 768 (UDP), 792 (ICMP), 3927 (link-local addresses).
- types: `udpip_peer_t`, `udpip_t`
- constants: `UDPIP_BROADCAST` = 0xFFFFFFFFu
- `void udpip_init(udpip_t *u, const uint8_t mac[6], uint32_t ip, uint32_t mask, uint16_t port, uint32_t group, udpip_send_fn send, udpip_recv_fn recv, void *ctx)`
- `void udpip_input(udpip_t *u, const uint8_t *frame, int len)` — A received frame (without FCS). Calls recv for each UDP datagram to our port, answers ARP and ping.
- `int udpip_send(udpip_t *u, const udpip_peer_t *to, const uint8_t *data, int len)` — Sends a UDP datagram from our port to a peer (to->mac all 0xFF and to->ip UDPIP_BROADCAST for a broadcast). Returns 0, or -1 if it does not fit in one frame.
- `uint32_t udpip_link_local(uint32_t id)` — A link-local address 169.254.1.0 .. 169.254.254.255 (RFC 3927) and a locally administered unicast MAC (02:xx:...), both derived from a board id, so a board keeps them across resets.
- `void udpip_mac_from_id(uint32_t id, uint8_t mac[6])`
- `uint16_t udpip_checksum(uint32_t sum, const uint8_t *p, int n)` — The Internet checksum (RFC 1071) of n bytes, added to sum (pass 0).

## `midi/usbdesc.h`
what a USB host needs from a MIDI device's descriptors: the configuration to select and the IN endpoints of its MIDIStreaming interfaces (USB 2.0 spec. sec. 9.6; USB Device Class Definition for MIDI Devices 1.0, sec. 6: interface class 1 audio, subclass 3 MIDIStreaming, bulk endpoints of 4-byte packets). Platform independent: the board's USB host (target/h745/app/m4/usbh_midi.c) feeds it the bytes it read.
- types: `usbdesc_midi_t`, `usbdesc_device_t`
- `int usbdesc_device(const uint8_t *d, int len, usbdesc_device_t *out)`
- `int usbdesc_config_total(const uint8_t *d, int len)` — wTotalLength of a configuration descriptor (its first 9 bytes at least), 0 if not one.
- `int usbdesc_find_midi(const uint8_t *d, int len, usbdesc_midi_t *out)` — Walks a whole configuration descriptor (wTotalLength bytes; a shorter read is walked as far as it goes). Keeps the IN endpoints (bulk or interrupt) of the MIDIStreaming interfaces at alternate setting 0. Returns the n...
- `int usbdesc_string(const uint8_t *d, int len, char *out, int out_size)` — A string descriptor (UTF-16LE) as printable ASCII in out (others become '?'), NUL-terminated. Returns its length, 0 if not a string descriptor.
